caption: The worked example: a 448-bit message gets one 1 bit, then 511 zeros, then a 64-bit length, so the padded length is 1024 bits — exactly two 512-bit blocks. The two highlighted steps are the bits students most often forget.

spec.title: Padding a 448-bit message (L = 448)
spec.aria: A 448-bit message is padded with one 1 bit, 511 zero bits and a 64-bit length to reach 1024 bits, which is two 512-bit blocks; each block runs 64 compression rounds and the result is a 256-bit digest.
